title: Decision Trace Compactifier and Hop Metrics Retention
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Smart routing produces verbose per-request decision state (region choice, tier, model variant fallback traces) and high-cardinality per-hop micro-metrics. This increases storage costs and slows queries for RCA and SLO analysis. We need a scheme to compact decision traces, retain useful hop metrics for SLOs, and make sampled full-context snapshots available for deep debugging.

Goals:
- Reduce routing telemetry storage by ~6x for regular request streams while preserving the ability to reconstruct decision rationale for sampled sessions.
- Provide per-hop aggregated metrics (p90/p99 latency, fallback counts, model-variant transitions) retained for 90 days for SLO dashboards.
- Maintain an accessible path to full decision snapshots (prefix + KV state + policy rationale) for traced requests (1 in 10k by default) with configurable sampling.

Proposal:
1) Compact trace envelope: replace raw per-hop blobs with a canonicalized compact envelope: fixed fields (route_id, chosen_region, chosen_tier, final_model_variant, reason_codes) + diffs (small list of deltas for hops that diverged from defaults). Store envelope as JSONL with a compressed prefix and a small checksum for integrity.
2) Hop metric rollups: produce a per-minute rollup keyed by (region,tier,model_variant,route_id) containing counters and aggregated latency percentiles using t-digest. Ingest these into the rollup store (Prometheus+long-term TS DB pattern) for 90-day retention and dashboarding.
3) Snapshot store: fully materialize full decision traces to an archival blob store (S3/GCS) but only for sampled requests. Index snapshots by trace_id and include a tiny linked reference in the compact envelope. Snapshot retention will be configurable by customer/owner.
4) Backfill/migration: for past 30 days create a short-lived migration pipeline that compacts recently-stored verbose traces into the new envelope format; large payloads are moved to snapshot store if they exceed size thresholds.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Full-text indexing vs canonical envelopes: full indexing supports richer ad-hoc queries but multiplies storage. We chose canonical envelopes + rollups to minimize cost and keep query paths fast for SRE and on-call flows.
- More aggressive sampling: lowering sample rate reduces cost but increases time-to-repro. We default to 1/10k and provide per-customer overrides for high-risk tenants.
- Inline snapshots in trace DB vs external blob: external blob reduces DB load and simplifies retention policies; it requires a secure lookup path for audits (KMS-protected references).

Instrumentation changes:
- Router: emit compact envelope instead of full hop array by default. Add snapshot upload hook for sampled traces.
- Ingest pipeline: new compactifier service to dedupe reason_codes, compute checksums, and emit rollup metrics.
- Observability UI: new "Routing Rollups" dashboard with hop-level aggregated p50/p90/p99, fallback trend, and region/tier heatmaps.

Operational concerns:
- Security: snapshots contain sensitive routing context and must be encrypted (KMS/HSM) and access-audited. Security review required (see security_review_required).
- Cost estimate: projected 0.65x net increase in snapshot storage for sampled flows, and 0.17x reduction in DB storage cost after migration. Marketing/procurement to validate pricing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compact envelopes are produced for >=99% of incoming routing requests in canary region.
- Rollup metrics are available in dashboard with correct region/tier aggregation and match raw-sample-derived baselines within 3% for p90.
- Snapshot retrieval path (trace_id -> blob) completed within 1s for on-call flows.

References and artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RO/Decision+Compactifier, GH RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/728, spike notes: drive: drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RoutingSpike
